page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Daldv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 16 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 1890 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are present, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core and multi-core CPU performance. The server achieves top 25% results in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU encryption tests. Image processing and text processing benchmarks also rank in the top 25%. For small language model inference using a 135M model, the server demonstrates top 10% text generation speeds at 344.97 tokens per second and top 25% prompt processing speeds. Multi-core stress-ng, Passmark database operations, and memory bandwidth tests fall within the middle 50% average category.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D32alds_v6 is designed for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints, representing a low-memory, compute-dense hardware profile. This resource density offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads where CPU performance is the primary bottleneck rather than RAM capacity. The bundled 1890 GB local storage provides high-capacity local disk access, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training. Suitable workloads include software compilation, text and image processing, web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
